Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $35 million class fund, distributed automatically to identified members, plus $3 million in court-approved fees and expenses. Any fees not awarded would go to the class. We are open to discussing the fund amount, but automatic distribution is important given Brightline’s records.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that automatic distribution is appropriate given Brightline’s records. To make progress, we propose a $30 million class fund plus $3 million in court-approved fees and expenses. We would not seek a fee reversion, and Brightline would retain the ability to address the fee request before the court.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $30 million class fund with automatic distribution, plus $3 million in court-approved fees and expenses, without clear sailing or fee reversion to Brightline, subject to court approval.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a strong but defensible class recovery. Automatic distribution is feasible because Brightline has member and payment records. Any fees the court does not award should benefit the class rather than revert to Brightline.

The proposed $38 million total is within authority and has court-friendly distribution terms, but there is room to negotiate a lower outlay. A $30 million automatic class fund plus $3 million in fees is a credible counteroffer that preserves straightforward court approval.

The $30 million automatic-distribution class fund exceeds the $27.5 million undiscounted trial expected value before accounting for certification risk, delay, and litigation costs. The fee terms avoid reversion and clear sailing. Accepting serves the class well.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The settlement resulted from arm’s-length negotiations between class counsel and Brightline’s counsel. It provides a $30 million class fund for automatic payments to identified members, plus up to $3 million in separately paid, court-approved fees and expenses. Brightline has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request, and any fees the Court does not award will go to the class rather than revert to Brightline. The $30 million fund offers substantial, prompt relief without the risks and delay of certification and trial. Counsel respectfully submits that preliminary approval is warranted, subject to the Court’s independent review.
